shape.text: Dropbox's token endpoint reference shows an example response for a legacy long-lived access token with no expires_in member and no refresh_token member, unlike its short-lived examples.
Dropbox states a prefix, alphabet or length for the legacy long-lived access token.

unresolved.reason: Dropbox treats access tokens as opaque and states no format for this form; the one rule artifact on record has no independent second artifact.

issuance.text: A Dropbox developer blog post dated Sep 17, 2020 states creation of long-lived access tokens would be retired on September 30th, 2021, and an undated update says new ones are no longer offered.

lifecycle.text: Dropbox's pages agree on one date for the end of long-lived token availability.

unresolved.reason: The guide says until mid 2021 and the blog says September 30th, 2021; the pages do not reconcile them.

lifecycle.text: Dropbox states when, or whether, an already issued long-lived access token stops authenticating.

unresolved.reason: No page read states it and no token was tested.

collisions.text: A provider statement separates legacy long-lived tokens from short-lived tokens by shape.

unresolved.reason: Dropbox says tokens are opaque; the separation here rests on the documented issuance and expiry difference only.
